properties.value: Bitcoin tutorial (比特币教程-理论) code that manually constructs the secp256k1 curve with the python-ecdsa library and generates a real Bitcoin keypair from it (secret = os.urandom(32), public point = secret*G). properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Digest comparisons in the two Go consensus demos (DPoS and PoS): consecutive-block SHA-256 hashes compared with != for chain-link validation. Genuinely non-constant-time digest comparisons, but both operands are public block hashes, so the timing-leak claim is theoretical rather than exploitable. properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA-256 is the workhorse hash across this whole repository: block hashing and PoW mining in the Bitcoin tutorial chapters (sha256.Sum256 over block headers and PoW data), merkle-tree construction, transaction-ID hashing, Bitcoin address derivation (SHA-256 → RIPEMD-160 double-hash), and block/consensus hashing in the PBFT, DPoS and PoS demos (sha256.New + Write + Sum). Python hashlib.sha256 examples in the theory chapter. SHA-256 is not Shor-broken; Grover halves preimage to 128-bit, acceptable.

The EVM bytecode embedded in these build artifacts uses the KECCAK256/SHA3 opcode (Ethereum's pre-standardization Keccak-256, whose padding differs from FIPS-202 SHA3-256) for function-selector derivation, mapping keys and storage indexing. This is the Ethereum platform hash — observable here, replaceable only by the EVM. Grover halves preimage resistance t

properties.value: Secure randomness sources for the Bitcoin tutorials: Go rand.Reader feeds ecdsa.GenerateKey and ecdsa.Sign (transaction signatures) across the four chapter copies; Python os.urandom(32) generates the secp256k1 private key in ec-math.py. These are the correct CSPRNGs — no weakness; recorded so the inventory shows where key material entropy comes from. Changeable here only in the sense that tutorial code could be modernized; nothing to fix.
